name: Ninam
confidence_why: Migliazza 1972 assigns primary stress to the penultimate vowel of the word (the last vowel only in monosyllables), whereas the catalog's final-stress coding rests on StressTyp2's reading, via Hyman 1977, of Migliazza and Grimes 1961, where final stress holds only for phrase-medial feet and the foot before a pause is itself penultimate.
catalog_quote: Utterances are divided into stress groups or feet; stress will occur on the final syllable of a foot, unless that foot occurs before a pause, then stress will be on the penultimate of the foot. (Hyman 1977:42)

tone_statements.citation: Ferreira, Helder Perri. 2010. Bibliografia comentada. Produto do Projeto de Documentação da Língua Ninam (Prodoclin, Museu do Índio-FUNAI / UNESCO Projeto 914BRA4010), agosto de 2010. Rio de Janeiro: Museu do Índio. 18 pp. [PDF 'Ninam_bibliogr_comentada_sitev3rev']
tone_statements.quote: Procuram identificar as diferenças nos padrões tonais do PE silábico ideofónico e não-ideofónico. Estudam ainda a ocorrência de <plus juncture> tanto no interior como na fronteira silábica. Distinguem as características dos chamados grupos (segmentos) de contorno e grupos (segmentos) de pausa, ressaltando a óbvia importância do primeiro na estruturação do sistema de entonação. Apresentam ainda os quatro tons não-fonêmicos observados na língua e, por fim, discutem alguns de seus usos como diacríticos fonológicos em contexto conversacional.
tone_statements.translation: They seek to identify the differences in the tonal patterns of ideophonic and non-ideophonic syllabic feet. They also study the occurrence of <plus juncture> both inside and at the boundary of the syllable. They distinguish the characteristics of the so-called contour groups (segments) and pause groups (segments), stressing the obvious importance of the former in structuring the intonation system. They further present the four non-phonemic tones observed in the language and, finally, discuss some of their uses as phonological diacritics in conversational context.
tone_statements.locator: entry 'MIGLIAZZA, E. & GRIMES, J. E. 1961. Sciriana phonology' (unpaginated report)
tone_statements.summary: Secondhand (after M&G 1961): no lexical tone; four non-phonemic pitch levels belong to contour-level intonation; feet carry stress.

audit.recode_to: fixed penultimate, dominant (penultimate stress; secondary stress two vowels to the left), citing Migliazza 1972:161-162 (A.P.1/A.P.2) as deciding source and M&G 1961:35,37 as the phrase-level surface description; add caution: word-final unstressed vowels elide/devoice at non-pause word boundaries (1972:166-167), so phrase-medial words surface with final stress — the basis of StressTyp2/WALS 'ultimate'. Domain stays word and phrase together/phrase-sensitive; keep out of the strict set. If the catalog prefers not to reclassify on one author's reanalysis, minimum action is re-read-with-listed-source (Migliazza 1972, held) and cite both.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding sentences are verbatim in the 1961 scan we hold at p.35 and p.37 (page scan and text read). sources.quote: p. 35: "Every foot also has one loud stress. This occurs on the penault [sic] or ultima of the foot — on the penult of a foot that is at the end of a pause group, on the ultima of all other feet. Accordingly, the minimum foot that can occur at the end of a pause group is a two-syllable one, whereas the minimum foot that can occur elsewhere is a one-syllable one." p. 37: "Paroxytonic feet occur only at the end of pause groups; all other feet are oxytonic."

sources.quote: p.161: 'Primary stress is assigned to the penultimate vowel of underlying phonological words.' p.162 A.P.1: 'primary stress is assigned on the penultimate vowel of a word and to the last vowel if the word is monosyllabic. The rule A.P.1 as specified would not assign stress with just a morpheme boundary, but would assign it with word and pause boundary.' A.P.2: 'secondary stress is placed on the second vowel preceding the primary stressed vowel.' tone.quote: O sufixo /-p/ ocorre também em formação de nomes compostos, segundo Gale (1990), os quais se diferenciam do sintagma nominal por haver um acento primário e um secundário nos nomes que os compõem, enquanto que os nomes em um sintagma nominal mantêm seu acento primário.
tone.translation: The suffix /-p/ also occurs in the formation of compound nouns, according to Gale [Goodwin Gómez] (1990), which differ from the noun phrase in having one primary and one secondary accent on the nouns that compose them, whereas the nouns in a noun phrase keep their primary accent.
tone.summary: No tone mentioned; word stress with primary vs secondary accent distinguishing compounds from phrases (after Goodwin Gómez 1990).
